articles.title: Checker Flag Subtle
articles.summary: Faint warped checker ghost in spec only; soft cells, gentle wobble, low contrast sheen. A faint gingham shimmer in the bright part of panels; from a distance the cells merge to a quiet sheen, no flag read.
articles.what: Faint warped checkered-flag specular ghost — soft-edged alternating cells with a gentle FBM wobble so the grid never sits perfectly straight, R=Metallic Up close: Small soft-edged checker cells, about 12 px, alternating bright and dark in the shine, with a slight wobble so rows are not ruler straight. Barely visible on satin; clearly checkered inside the highlight on metallic. From a distance: A faint gingham shimmer in the bright part of panels; from a distance the cells merge to a quiet sheen, no flag read. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Racing & Livery Story (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: body, hood, under stripes.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Racing & Livery Story", or search for "Checker Flag Subtle".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood and roof on dark metallic bases so the ghost shows
Under racing stripes for a themed undertone
Numbers read fine; the ghost is too weak to compete with them.
Almost nothing, a trace of checker in the highlight band
Pairs well with: gloss, metallic, matte.
pitfalls: Not a checker paint pattern: it adds no black and white squares
Not carbon weave: cells are square and alternate, no twill
Avoid: high-contrast base colors, busy graphic overlays.
articles.intent_note: A spec pattern changes the shine only: metal, roughness and clearcoat, never the paint colour.
articles.paint_advice: It cannot recolour anything. Metal added to a light paint looks bright; metal added to a dark paint stays dark, because metal reflection inherits the paint colour. Pair it with a paint that gives the gloss difference something to show on.

combos.why: Up to five overlays stack in order; a strong overlay can wash out the ones below it.
The blend mode decides how this overlay meets the base shine. Normal is the safe start.
Coat values 1 to 15 and roughness under 15 on non-chrome pixels are raised to safe values on export.

examples.title: Add it as an overlay
examples.goal: Layer Checker Flag Subtle over a base finish.
examples.result: The shine of the zone gets this texture while the colours stay put.

articles.title: Heat Discoloration
articles.summary: Concentric heat-tint bands with oxide micro-texture; subtle sparkle, bluing gradient zones. Reads as a liquid, rippled sheen that looks like heat haze or watered silk; the waves stay visible on larger panels.
articles.what: Heat-treated metal color zones — concentric temperature gradient bands like exhaust manifold bluing or weld heat-affected zones with oxide micro-texture Up close: Flowing wavy interference ripples, like heat shimmer or moire watermarks, with fine ridges 10-20 px apart curving and merging inside the highlight band. Soft rather than sharp; the same wavy bands appear on both halves, clearer on metal. From a distance: Reads as a liquid, rippled sheen that looks like heat haze or watered silk; the waves stay visible on larger panels. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Racing & Livery Story (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
when: Best on: hood, sides, hero panel.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Racing & Livery Story", or search for "Heat Discoloration".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Hood, roof, doors: waves need open panels to flow
Exhaust-adjacent rear areas if themed

pitfalls: Not heat-tint colour: despite the name it adds no blue or straw colour, only shine ripples
Not brushed metal: the ripples curve and merge, no straight grain
Avoid: very subtle on matte, may not read on dark colors.

articles.title: Salt Spray Corrosion
articles.summary: Faint clustered micro-pits with halo staining; subtle rough salt-air degradation. Gone at distance: plain base finish with a hint of blotchy weathering.
articles.what: Fine salt-air corrosion pitting — coastal marine environment surface degradation with clustered micro-pits, halo staining, and salt-exposure base roughness Up close: Sparse irregular clumps of tiny pixel-like specks, 20-40 px across, scattered unevenly like salt crust or pitting. A few clusters brighten the highlight; in the shadow floor they show as dark speckled patches. Nothing between the clusters. Looks natural and random, not geometric. From a distance: Gone at distance: plain base finish with a hint of blotchy weathering. No rust colour appears, it is shine only. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Weather, Wear & Track (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker). Texture detail: micro.
how: Click a zone card and expand SPEC OVERLAYS.
Click + ADD SPEC OVERLAY, open the Legacy collection tab and the group "Weather, Wear & Track", or search for "Salt Spray Corrosion".
Click it, then click Add this overlay in the Inspect surface window.
Set Strength (default 50%) and tick the Metallic, Roughness and Clearcoat boxes you want.
Use Size and Rotation to make the texture finer, then render.
tips: Rockers, bumpers and lower sides: where salt spray hits
Trim and chrome for an aged look
Numbers keep their colour; scattered clumps only rarely land on numerals.
A few faint speckled patches in the highlight, subtle
Pairs well with: matte, satin, metallic.
pitfalls: Not rust colour: spec only, the red tag is not shown
Not uniform grain: it is clumpy and sparse, with empty gaps

articles.title: Vinyl Stretched
articles.summary: Directional micro-streaks with periodic ridges; smooth stretched sheen, low contrast, subtle banding. Reads as plain smooth satin or metal; the specks disappear completely.
articles.what: Vinyl wrap stretched over a curve — directional micro-streaks along the stretch axis with periodic ridges where film thinned and thickened, G=Roughness Up close: Almost smooth: a very fine scatter of tiny short specks, 1-3 px, mostly slanted slightly, visible only inside the highlight on metallic. No periodic ridges or banding can be seen at 1:1; satin shows nearly nothing. From a distance: Reads as plain smooth satin or metal; the specks disappear completely. It changes the shine only, never the colour. Channels it touches: the channels set by its defaults. Group: Racing & Livery Story (Legacy collection tab of the spec overlay picker).
